title: Split integration tests by runtime, add \"smoke\" PR job and nightly full-suite orchestration
author: Marisol Ortega
release_notes: CI: Split integration jobs by runtime (Python/Node/Go), introduce lightweight PR 'smoke' test, nightly full integration orchestration. Reduced concurrency and flakiness; pinned key actions and improved cache keys for deps/containers.
description:
Context: Our monolithic integration.yml has grown slow and brittle; PR pipelines are expensive and noisy and full-suite nightly runs are hard to reason about. Motivation: speed up PR feedback (fast failure for obvious regressions), reduce flake surface area by isolating runtime-specific dependencies, and centralize orchestration for full end-to-end nightly validation. What this PR does: 1) Splits the large integration workflow into three runtime-specific workflows: .github/workflows/integration-python.yml, integration-node.yml, integration-go.yml. Each workflow focuses on runtime build/install/test for the service matrix that touches that runtime. 2) Adds a lightweight .github/workflows/integration-smoke-pr.yml that runs a minimal smoke matrix on every PR (unit+basic integration scenarios, DB migrations, API health) to give fast signal. 3) Adds .github/workflows/integration-nightly-orchestrator.yml which triggers the full cross-runtime suites sequentially during off-peak hours and posts a summary to #ci-notifications. 4) Introduces a small composite action .github/actions/integration-setup to consolidate environment bootstrap (docker compose up, env var validation, KMS secret fetch shim) and avoid duplication across workflows. 5) Reduces concurrency by using per-repo concurrency groups and resource classes: workflows now use concurrency: group: integration-${{ github.ref }} and a slimmer default max-parallel=2 for matrix jobs to limit noisy bursts. 6) Improves caching (cache keys include lockfile hash and a docker-layer stamp) and pins checkout/setup action SHAs to reduce subtle CI drift. 7) Fixes a docker-compose race observed in CI by adding deterministic teardown and a small retry/backoff for container stop/cleanup.
Checklist: - [x] split workflows and added smoke job - [x] composite setup action implemented - [x] cache key and action pinning - [x] add nightly orchestrator and channel notifications - [x] run full test battery locally and in staging CI - [x] update docs/ci/README.md with workflow descriptions
Commits (high level): - feat(ci): create integration-smoke-pr.yml and minimal test matrix - feat(ci): split integration workflows by runtime (python/node/go) - refactor(ci): add composite integration-setup action, pin actions - fix(ci): add deterministic docker teardown + retry/backoff - chore(ci): update README and add notification hook
Tests / CI: Initial run (2025-11-20): smoke matrix passed but full python integration failed intermittently due to docker-compose teardown race (containers not removed quickly enough). Added fix in second commit (deterministic teardown + small sleep and retry). Rerun (2025-11-22): all checks green except a transient lint flake that was unrelated to changes; lint re-run passed. Final CI status: pass.
Changed areas (representative files): .github/workflows/integration-smoke-pr.yml, .github/workflows/integration-python.yml, .github/workflows/integration-node.yml, .github/workflows/integration-go.yml, .github/workflows/integration-nightly-orchestrator.yml, .github/actions/integration-setup/action.yml, ci/scripts/docker-teardown.sh, ci/cache-helpers.sh, docs/ci/README.md, package.json (test tweaks), go.mod (test helper), python/requirements-dev.txt (pinned deps)
Review conversation (summary): - Ethan: "Nice split — can we avoid duplicating the env validation logic?" -> Author: "Moved to composite action integration-setup; reduced duplication and documented interface." - Priya: "Nightly orchestration looks good but we should gate notifications on failure only." -> Author: "Updated orchestrator to only post to #ci-notifications on failure and include a short digest on success to avoid noise." - Liam: "Lockfile/hash for cache keys looks promising; ensure npm and pip keys don't collide." -> Author: "Added runtime-scoped cache keys (node-<hash>, python-<hash>, go-<hash>)." - Priya (follow-up): "Observed one remaining flake re: port collision on GH runners." -> Author: "Added ephemeral port reservation via ci/scripts/port-allocator and configured docker-compose to use that port; verified in staging."
Merge notes: After approvals from Ethan and Priya and green CI, PR was merged via squash on 2025-11-25.
Post-merge steps taken: - Nightly orchestrator scheduled and smoke job enabled on all teams. - Updated internal CI docs and an FYI in #platform-ops.
Potential follow-ups (captured in ENG-1301): - Replace composer/docker-layer stamp with a reproducible image hash upload for faster restores. - Evaluate splitting nightlies by service boundaries for further parallelism.
Links: Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1254, Staging CI run: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/98765. Notes: This PR focuses on CI hygiene and developer velocity; no production code logic changed beyond test scaffolding. If any runtime integration failures appear after this change, the nightly orchestrator provides a single source of truth for reproducing the full suite.
commits: feat(ci): create smoke PR job and basic matrix
feat(ci): split integration workflows by runtime
refactor(ci): extraction of integration-setup composite action
review_comments: Ethan: Move env validation into composite action to avoid duplication.
Priya: Gate notifications from nightly orchestrator to failure-only or low-volume digests.
Liam: Make cache keys runtime-scoped to avoid collisions.
Priya: Add ephemeral port allocator to avoid GH runner port collisions.
